articles.title: 65 Years Later, The Greatest 'Peanuts' Comic Strip Ever is Still an Adorable Masterpiece
articles.summary: Seventeen thousand, eight hundred and ninety-seven. That’s how many Peanuts comics Charles Schulz created over the 50 years that he wrote and drew his beloved comic strip. Peanuts debuted on Oct. 2, 1950, began publishing Sunday strips on Jan. 6, 1952, and concluded its legendary run on Feb.
body: At first, I thought maybe it would make sense to go for the first comic strip or the last one. Both of those comics are really important to the history of Peanuts, but if you actually read them, neither represents the very best the strip has to offer.

Peanuts didn't arrive fully-formed. It took Charles Schulz a while to develop its characters and find their iconic look. That’s clear in the very first comic strip, which features the characters Shermy and Patty (not Peppermint Patty, just Patty) in a starring role and Charlie Brown in a supporting one. Charlie Brown also doesn’t quite look like himself yet. For these reasons, it can’t be the first one.

The last one isn’t perfect either because, unlike, say, Calvin and Hobbes, Peanuts didn’t end because its artist was ready to conclude their story. Bill Watterson’s readiness to end Calvin and Hobbes motivated him to craft a beautiful ending for the characters. Peanuts, in contrast, ended because Charles Schulz got incredibly sick and was no longer able to carry on. And while the last strip — which is basically just Schulz’s goodbye letter to fans — is moving, it isn’t some deeply satisfying ending for the characters.
points: That’s how many Peanuts comics Charles Schulz created over the 50 years that he wrote and drew his beloved comic strip.

articles.title: "We have to go a different path" - Krafton thinks PUBG Ded.Net's pulpy gameshow hyperviolence and roguelite twist can make it the next big battle royale
articles.summary: Player Unknown's Battlegrounds is arguably one of the most important games to release in the past decade. If H1Z1 built the foundation of the battle royale genre, PUBG certainly shaped it into the form that remains hugely successful today.
body: Fortnite might have stolen the battle royale crown, but PUBG's name still means something even today. So when publisher Krafton announced a brand-new PUBG was in the works last month, it was an immediately exciting prospect for battle royale fans. And doubtless a daunting one for its development team, given the large shoes Ded.Net has to fill.

But what does it mean to make a new PUBG in the shadow of the original? How do you make something familiar, while keeping it fresh enough that it doesn't feel redundant? The answer may lie in Ded.Net; a grungy splatterfest being developed by Krafton's Wisconsin studio, PUBG Madison, that gives those battle royale fundamentals a more rogue-like spin. To find out more, I spoke with creative director Dave Curd about the challenges and opportunities facing the team.

"I was charged with spreading the gospel of PUBG to an audience that might not already appreciate it or like it or understand it," Curd told me at Gamescom. And that required breaking it down to its fundamentals. "What is PUBG? Is it a blue Zone? Is it the level three helmet? I think [it's] desperate survival. I think it's survival of the fittest, it's dog eat dog."
points: Player Unknown's Battlegrounds is arguably one of the most important games to release in the past decade.
If H1Z1 built the foundation of the battle royale genre, PUBG certainly shaped it into the form that remains hugely successful today.

articles.title: 5 Perfect Animated Movies on Netflix Better Than 'KPop Demon Hunters'
articles.summary: KPop Demon Hunters debuted on Netflix in June 2025, and in short order, everyone lost their minds. The movie received hundreds of millions of views and even made its way into theaters, a very rare feat for a Netflix Original that started out on the streaming platform.
body: I get it. The songs are incredibly catchy and the movie is funnier and more action-packed than anybody could have expected. But while everyone is still so excited about KPop Demon Hunters, I’d like to point out that there are other — and, dare I say, better — animated movies on Netflix as well. There are films that have stood the test of time, others that managed to bring something new to longstanding fandoms, and plenty of straight-to-Netflix flicks that didn’t make quite the same splash, but are still arguably superior.
So if you’re at all fatigued by KPop Demon Hunter -mania, I invite you to scroll right past it on Netflix and check out these five animated masterpieces instead.

KPop Demon Hunters and The Mitchells vs. the Machines actually have quite a bit in common. Both are animated films that were produced by Sony Pictures Animation and were released directly onto Netflix. The Mitchells vs. the Machines reached over 50 million views on the platform within its first month, which doesn’t really compare to the mega-hit of KPop Demon Hunters. And yet, it was easily one of the biggest releases during the pandemic.

articles.title: Naruto Teasers Reveal New Shadow Rising Manga and Anime Crossover Series
articles.summary: Naruto is alive and well, as author Masashi Kishimoto has announced a new manga called Shadow Rising – and a new anime crossover series is on the way, too. Both Naruto projects were announced during the Naruto panel at New York Comic Con 2026.
body: The panel did come with more information about that anime series, though. Aptly titled "Naruto x Ninku," the show will serve as a full-on crossover between Naruto and popular '90s manga and anime franchise Ninku. Both the show and the manga did receive teaser trailers, which you can see below.

"Team 7 members Naruto, Sasuke, and Sakura are given a mission by Kakashi," an official description for Naruto x Ninku said. "Since Kakashi cannot participate himself, Naruto is appointed acting leader. As a result of this decision, Naruto is fully motivated to make the mission a success. However, on the way, Team 7 finds themselves lost in another world. What appears before the bewildered trio is a boy with a face resembling a frog’s, named Fūsuke. What awaits them in this strange new world?"

Meanwhile, as reported by Variety, the Naruto panel also came with a surprise update on the live-action movie. Amid rumors of early plot details and casting decisions, director Destin Daniel Cretton shared a message where he explained "what an honor it is to bring Kishimoto-sensei's incredible world and characters to life."

articles.summary: Prime Video has published a new Blade Runner 2099 trailer, revealing more about the mystery surrounding its missing Replicants, as well as the roles Hunter Schafer and Michelle Yeoh play in the story.
body: This more detailed look at the Amazon-backed limited series and its dystopian sci-fi setting arrived at New York Comic Con 2026. Attendees at the Blade Runner 2099 panel were treated to the new trailer in person, with both it and a new poster now available for all to see online.
Starring Schafer (Euphoria) and Yeoh (Everything Everywhere All at Once) as Cora and Olwen, respectively, Blade Runner 2099 is set to premiere in November. You can see the NYCC 2026 trailer below.

"Fifty years after the events of Blade Runner 2049, Los Angeles has been reborn, just not by humanity," an official description from Prime Video said. "Cora, a fugitive in a final bid to stop running, takes on one last identity: a Blade Runner. Forced to partner with Olwen, a Replicant days from dying, she hunts down a runaway hiding a truth that could collapse a fragile city."

articles.summary: Sundays are for realising that this is speeder racing. No, not podracing. You're not skilled enough for that yet. You've got to get your reps in to be the best of the best on the tracks of the galaxy far, far away. You've got to beat Ary Quill, Griff Halloran, Soren Zaks, Katja Mox, and the rest.
body: Oh, you're challenging him to a race? Prefer to be BIDDYLASTED INTO OBLIVION.

Right off the start, Biddy BIDDYLASTS his way into first place aboard his trusty speeder bike. You take off after him in your landspeeder. Your ramjet boost finally warms up as you zig-zag around looming rocks. You activate it. Immediately, a wall of text is shot into your eyeballs. You make out a name. Connor Makar. Then Eurogamer blue-tinged a vision of a Smashmouth video-worthy face.

The burst of speed propels you a bit closer to Biddy just as the road snakes into a labyrinbthine cave complex. Seeing that he's in range, but scrabble for your ion bolt. It fires, but racer-seeking jolt of enery somehow misses as Biddy disappears over the edge of a jump. You realise too late that you're about to hit a mine he's dropped. As it rocks your craft, shards of words are flicked into your eyeballs. You make out the word Respec, and realise you've been inflicted with some Knowledge about the current state of games media.
"With Respec, we are lucky – we can take our time and slowly build that startup because its overheads are covered in the profit margins of a long-established, defensively budgeted business.

articles.title: Gary Larson's 10 Greatest 'Far Side' Comics, Ranked
articles.summary: What, exactly, is the measure of greatness when it comes to comic strips? The daily newspaper comic is a very limiting art form, with only a few panels — sometimes just one panel — to make a joke.
body: Yet, we’ve seen comic strips do so much more than that. Characters like Snoopy and Garfield have become part of the fabric of our culture. Comic strips are capable of greatness. And since greatness is possible, what, then, makes a comic strip great?

The first instinct is to go for something “deep.” Comic strips like Peanuts and Calvin and Hobbes occasionally ventured outside of comedy to examine the world and say something thoughtful about it. But that’s not the case for other comic strips that don’t go deep. For Garfield, I’d argue greatness would come down to a really clever, relatable gag. For something like Prince Valiant, which specialized in highly detailed, picturesque images, I imagine greatness would relate to visual appeal.
So what would the measure of greatness be for Gary Larson’s The Far Side?
points: What, exactly, is the measure of greatness when it comes to comic strips?
The daily newspaper comic is a very limiting art form, with only a few panels — sometimes just one panel — to make a joke.
Yet, we’ve seen comic strips do so much more than that.
Characters like Snoopy and Garfield have become part of the fabric of our culture.

articles.title: Forget a 'Halloween' Rewatch, Dan Stevens' Best Horror Movie Is a Slasher Surprise
articles.summary: Wingard's latest also came with an intriguing caveat that may have been a turnoff for casual theatergoers: Onslaught exists in a shared universe with his previous indie horror flick, The Guest.
body: Familiarity with The Guest won't have any real impact on your ability to enjoy Onslaught, which is on VOD as of last week. (Dan Stevens plays two very different characters across the two films, and any connections are tenuous at best.) But if you've never seen Wingard's 2014 action thriller, it's still worth checking out as we sprint through our annual Halloween Countdown.

The Guest stars Dan Stevens as David Collins, a U.S. soldier who returns from Afghanistan on a benevolent mission. After his friend Caleb Peterson dies in battle, David arrives at the doorstep of Caleb's grieving family and offers to help out in any way he can. At least, that's what he claims.

Stevens is so charming in the role that, for most of the movie, David gets away with everything. Even the audience will likely be rooting for him… up to a certain point. Eventually it's revealed that ( spoiler alert ) David isn't who he claims to be.

articles.title: Arc Raiders' 2.0 Update and 'Spider-Man' Grappling Hook Drive Player Count to Reach 7-Month High
articles.summary: The new Arc Raiders 2.0 update has triggered a seven-month high for its concurrent player count on Steam as fans show up for its "Spider-Man" grappling hook, a new map, a free weekend, and more.
body: Embark's once-viral extraction experience has had a rough few months. As the studio slowed down updates and vowed to rework its divisive Expedition prestige system, Arc Raiders players have largely left it behind, hoping to one day return to Speranza should more enticing updates arrive.

After reaching an all-time peak of nearly 500,000 players on Steam (via SteamDB ), it's consistently struggled to reach more than 35,000 players on PC since July. It was a fall from grace that's left fans missing the honeymoon phase, but the Frozen Trail update, which launched two days ago, October 8, across PC, PlayStation 5, and Xbox Series X/S, has almost immediately brought back some of that hype.

In September, Arc Raiders reached a player count low of just 10,000 on Steam. As of the publication of this story, 166,670 people are logged onto Arc Raiders on the PC platform alone, and it looks like it could keep climbing. It's a number Embark hasn't hit since early April, and although it's too soon to tell if these are the kind of results needed to give it a proper second wind, it does mark the first time the game has achieved a notable spike since December 2025.
points: The new Arc Raiders 2.0 update has triggered a seven-month high for its concurrent player count on Steam as fans show up for its "Spider-Man" grappling hook, a new map, a free weekend, and more.

articles.title: Image Comics' Roam Reunites Paper Girls Creators Brian K. Vaughan and Cliff Chiang
articles.summary: In what is easily one of the most exciting comic book-related announcements to come out of NYCC 2026, IGN can exclusively reveal that Paper Girls creators Brian K. Vaughan and Cliff Chiang are reuniting for a new project at Image Comics.
body: “Cliff has already drawn the first several issues of ROAM, and I can’t wait for readers to see this breathtakingly original world he and our gifted collaborators Matt and Jared helped create," Vaughan tells IGN. "Thanks so much to the readers and retailers out here who are up for exploring something new with us!"

"There's no bigger thrill than breathing life into new worlds with your friends, that electric feeling of collaboration," Chiang says. "ROAM is unlike anything Brian and I have done before, but inspired by our love for comics as a medium. It's been a joy to reunite with our trusted teammates Matt Wilson and Jared Fletcher, and I'm incredibly grateful to Image Comics for continuing the creative partnership and exploration that began with Paper Girls. It's going to be a wild ride!"
Roam #1 will be released in February 2027, and it's already shaping up to be one of our most anticipated new comics of the eyar. You can preorder a copy at your local comic shop.
For more, check out IGN's original review of Paper Girls #1 and our review of Paper Girls Season 1.

articles.title: Strange Scaffold announces Gods With Badges, a tactics game where you decide when to switch off your bodycam
articles.summary: Strange Scaffold, the studio behind I Am Your Beast and El Paso, Elsewhere, has announced Gods With Badges, a narrative tactics game about the power police hold over life and death.
body: You play as Harrow McClellan, a disgraced police officer transferred back to her original post after the scandal that drove her out has become law enforcement legend. Every dialogue choice and turn-based encounter is a decision to play into that reputation or try to rise above it.

You'll patrol the open hubs of Scarhelm, a dystopian city of the future, seizing contraband, investigating complaints, and searching back alleys for evidence. Your dialogue choices, arrests, and uses of force shape Harrow's relationships with her fellow officers, the public, and the institutions around her.

Interestingly, when a situation escalates, the game shifts to isometric turn-based combat. Here you can take cover, rescue hostages, and decide how much force to use. You can also temporarily disable Harrow's body camera, unlocking new tactical and dialogue options but removing the public record of what happens next.

Gods With Badges began life as Hard Justice, an unrealised project from strategy studio Artificer. Strange Scaffold has built on its foundations and development materials, reinterpreting them in its own style.

articles.title: GTA 6 leaker threatens to upload a build with 'full story mode'
articles.summary: Cyberleek has been uploading footage of Grand Theft Auto 6 since August, most recently a 25-minute video featuring co-protagonist Jason totally nude. Given that GTA 6's November 19 release is just over a month away, on console at least, it seems natural that interest in these kinds of leaks would…
body: "Here's the deal, nice and clean. CYBERLEEK hits 30 million marketcap, the build goes out – full story mode, played to the end, credits and all. Don't believe it has full story mode? Ask for what you want to see, and it gets provided. Take-Two gets one way out: physical disks and a public apology. They can take it at any moment. Or they can gamble that CL is bluffing. Everyone knows which one they'll pick."

The other half of the deal suggests that publisher Take-Two Interactive could prevent this by releasing GTA 6 physically and apologizing, presumably for not releasing it on discs in the first place. Which will never happen, but does fit with Cyberleek's previous history of cosplay Robin Hood consumer rights complaints.

We know that Cyberleek has access to a playable build since one of the previous leaks ended with the word LEEK being machinegunned into a wall to prove the point. But an early build of GTA 6 seems like the worst possible way to play it on PC, though after the Xbox streaming thing turned out to be a bust, maybe there are people who don't want to wait?

articles.summary: In August, game director Chris Roberts said that Star Citizen's singleplayer component, Squadron 42, was being delayed out of 2026 to avoid clashing with Grand Theft Auto 6.
body: There's also a new trailer, which leans heavily on the oorah stuff that's always a bit of a turn-off in military science-fiction. Privateer was my favorite Wing Commander game because it left out all the Top Gun nonsense, but of course it's front-and-center in Squadron 42.

So too are the celebrity actors, with appearances by Mark Hamill, Gary Oldman, Rhona Mitra, that guy who played the Onion Knight in Game of Thrones, and other people who probably filmed most of their scenes a solid decade ago now. We also get to see a fair bit of the male version of the player-character, who will doubtless BroShep his way into most of the promos even though I'll be picking the one voiced by Alix Wilton Regan instead.

The Steam page lists Squadron 42's release date as Q2 2027, and I'd love to see it actually release on that date and be the solid combo of Wing Commander and Half-Life 2 that happens to have Gillian Anderson and Henry Cavill in the cutscenes that's being promised here. It could happen.

articles.title: GTA 6 leaker CyberLeek is now reportedly threatening to release a full, playable build of the game
articles.summary: A GTA 6 leaker has reportedly threatened to put out a complete, playable build of the game, start to finish.
body: The threat was posted on CyberLeek's website after the leaker shared 25 minutes of footage from the game earlier this week.

Rockstar has previously issued statements regarding the leaker, noting that the leaks are "heartbreaking" and that "this is obviously not how we intended for you to see the game after all this time". Take-Two, Rockstar's parent company, has been hunting for the person behind the leaks, and has tried to subpoena Discord for information pertaining to the leaker's identity.

After going quiet for a bit, CyberLeek came back with a bang this week, posting new footage from Rockstar's upcoming game that even features nude scenes, including a fully naked Jason, and a topless Lucia. Eurogamer has seen the video, and it appears to be legitimate - and, as is now traditional, has CyberLeek's emblem overlaid on top of the footage.
CyberLeek now reportedly says the build will go out if their cryptocurrency coin reaches a market cap of $30 million, and claims it can be played through to the end credits.

articles.title: Feature: Box Art Brawl - Duel: Wii Sports Resort
articles.summary: Which is the Wuhu winner? Hey everyone! Welcome to this week's edition of Box Art Brawl! Last time, we matched up a trio of covers for the GBA's Zone Of The Enders: The Fist Of Mars, though it wasn't a particularly close-fought contest.
body: This week, inspired by that big old Nintendo Switch Sports Resort overview trailer, we're taking a look at the game that inspired its namesake: Wii Sports Resort. This second entry in the 'Sports' series launched in 2009, offering up 12 different sports on Wuhu Island.
There are only two covers to choose between this week, so let's check 'em out.

The North American cover is all about showcasing what's new in the sequel. Most of the box is dedicated to four fresh sports, splitting things into quarters to highlight Swordplay, Wakeboarding, Archery and Basketball. It gets straight to the point, but a little creativity might not have gone amiss.

The European and Japanese design swings for something a little more original. We get a full-box piece of art, emphasising the new water sports in the foreground and some fresh beach activities in the back. It's maybe not quite as clear what's new as its NA counterpart, but we're sure most people would get the gist.

videos.title: The Witcher 3 Remastered - PC Performance Review
videos.summary: Unlike The Witcher 4, which has moved to Unreal Engine 5, The Witcher 3 Remastered sticks with CD Projekt Red’s own Red Engine, with more additions than a mage’s alchemy pot.
body: Here's our performance review of The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt Remastered and what we recommend for the optimal settings on PC.
points: Unlike The Witcher 4, which has moved to Unreal Engine 5, The Witcher 3 Remastered sticks with CD Projekt Red’s own Red Engine, with more additions than a mage’s alchemy pot.
It adds enhanced textures, improved foliage and Level of detail, better lighting with Ray and Path Tracing, DLSS 4.5 Ray Reconstruction, and much more.
However, this huge facelift still has its issues, with Nvidia HairWorks still killing framerates and potentially looking worse.

videos.summary: The Nintendo Switch Sports Resort game launches October 22, 2026, exclusively on the Nintendo Switch 2 system. Pre-orders are available now:
body: The latest game in the intuitive sports series is coming to Nintendo Switch 2!
Get moving solo or with family and friends across 12 immersive sports. Aim for the target’s center in Archery, knock down pins in Bowling, duke it out in Boxing, and more!
You can also explore the island! Use Joy-Con 2 mouse controls in Skateboarding, steer across the waves in Power Cruising, and tilt the controller to fly around freely in Prop Plane.
